title: RAW UNREVIEWED: an eight-slot source-fragment notebook with paid literal introductions and deterministic eviction
summary: A complete invented hand writer keeps only eight recent distinct fragments, each at most eight source characters. A fragment already in the notebook is written by its current slot; a new or evicted fragment is spelled in full. Explicit final marks retain every original word boundary. The reader builds the same notebook from the actual printed text, with no external phrase dictionary or plaintext oracle.

design.input_contract: Exact source tokens separated by single spaces, with explicit recipe boundaries. Lowercase a-z and the56 additional characters listed below are supported. Capitalization, listed punctuation, digits, word order and source-word boundaries are retained. Unlisted characters cause an explicit failure; they are never normalized away. Recipe start resets the notebook; ordinary line wraps and paragraphs inside a recipe do not. Repeated whitespace and exact physical source lineation are outside this teaching edition.
deterministic_fragments: For a token consisting solely of lowercase a-z, find maximal vowel runs over {a,e,i,o,u}. Cut immediately after every vowel run except the last. Keep the trailing consonants with the last piece. A token with zero or one vowel run stays one preliminary piece.
Any token containing uppercase, punctuation, digits or another listed additional character stays one preliminary piece.

Further divide any preliminary piece longer than eight source characters into consecutive eight-character pieces and one nonempty final remainder. This fixed cap bounds notebook storage, not a post-result fitted parameter.
The last fragment of the ORIGINAL source token gets END; every other fragment gets CONTINUE. Each fragment is one visible printed group. No source space is inferred from grammar.
design.notebook: Initially empty; at most eight distinct nonempty exact source-fragment strings, each of length at most eight. Slot0 is the most recently used fragment. After every fragment, remove its previous slot if present, insert it at slot0 and discard slot8 if the list would exceed eight. Maximum retained payload is64 source characters, plus row order; this is not merely eight possible states.
encode: If the next exact fragment is present, write its current slot code followed by END or CONTINUE. The literal branch is forbidden for a present fragment.
If absent, write NEW, the complete shared character encoding of the fragment, then END or CONTINUE. No fragment is assigned a private new permanent code.
Perform the notebook update only after writing the complete fragment. Identical fragments with different END/CONTINUE flags still share one notebook entry.
decode: A two-sign group whose first sign is one of the eight slot codes selects that currently occupied slot. Reject an empty slot, invalid final mark or extra body signs.

A group starting with NEW has a nonempty literal body between that initial sign and the final END/CONTINUE sign. Decode exactly that body using the shared character carrier; reject malformed units, more than eight recovered characters and a literal fragment already present in the notebook.

Append the recovered fragment to the pending source token, update the notebook identically, and finish the token only on END. A recipe or paragraph break with a pending unfinished source token is malformed; physical line wrapping alone leaves it pending.

After completing each token, replay the frozen segmentation rule to ensure its written fragment boundaries were canonical. No omitted word boundary, discretionary alternative split or source plaintext is needed.

concrete_carrier.lowercase_rule: Source a-s map in alphabetic order to ordinary_signs. Source t-z map to q followed by the first seven ordinary_signs. Thus every ordinary source character has a prefix-decodable one- or two-sign spelling.
concrete_carrier.additional_rule: For zero-based additional-character index j, write y plus rare_selectors[floor(j/8)] plus rare_selectors[j mod8]. Reject unused combinations.
concrete_carrier.framing: NEW r is absent from the literal character carrier. The visible group boundary identifies its final k/t mark, so a k or t inside the literal body is an ordinary carrier sign. Reference groups have exactly two signs; new-fragment groups have NEW, at least one encoded character unit, and one final mark.
concrete_carrier.scope: Only an artificial assignment of already familiar working drawing labels; no native atom, sound, word meaning, key or shape-role binding is asserted.

design.unfamiliar_and_repeated_inputs: Every unfamiliar word uses the same deterministic split and literal/reference rule. A single source character is a valid fragment. Repeated letters are retained inside fragments; repeated whole words are processed again in order and may use notebook references if their pieces remain present. Nothing is silently dropped or supplied from an external answer table.
design.learning_and_work: The learner pays for26 lowercase mappings,56 auxiliary-character mappings, eight slot labels, two final roles, NEW, the vowel/cap split rule and a movable eight-row notebook of at most64 source characters. Each fragment requires at most eight string comparisons and one row move. The notebook contents are carried by earlier paid literal output, not pre-shared message information.
design.exact_unequal_consequence: Once eight other distinct fragments have been used since a fragment's last use, that fragment has been evicted and must next be spelled literally. An immediately repeated fragment must use slot0 after its first occurrence. This eviction law differs from both a fixed letter permutation and a distance pointer into an arbitrarily long text.
design.smallest_falsifier: Use the abstract teaching sequence of nine distinct one-character fragments A through I, then A, then A again. The returning A must be introduced literally because it was evicted; the immediately following A must use slot0. An empty-slot reference at recipe start must be rejected. These are declared formal obligations, not an executed encoding test.
design.strongest_counterexample: A stream cycling through nine distinct fragments misses on every subsequent turn and pays the literal introducer and boundary mark repeatedly. Even with a short notebook, spelling cost can therefore dominate. Reference groups also end in only the two declared boundary shapes; a future literal native binding would have to face that strong restriction. No native fit is claimed.
design.cost_account: A reference costs two working signs. A new fragment pays NEW, every literal character unit, and one boundary sign; rare characters cost three signs each. All memory updates and the bounded scratch notebook are real hand-work costs. No target-shaped filler or unused decoration is inserted.
design.statistical_status: No source was encoded or counted and no manuscript data were accessed for this proposal. The symbolic slot meanings change with the reader's recovered notebook, so printed-group frequencies need not equal source-word or source-fragment frequencies. This is not a measured advantage.

predecessors.relation: Reuses an explicitly orthographic vowel-run segmentation, with a new fixed eight-character storage cap. The new mechanism is the transmitted bounded notebook, not a claim that changing chunk size repairs937 or identifies native syllables.

939 permutes a fixed26-letter alphabet. Here eight entries hold variable strings, can be absent, require paid literal introduction and are evicted. This is a different update/input contract, not another alphabet permutation.

The failed C arm indexed nearest prior whole-word distance up to503. This uses eight distinct capped fragments by current notebook rank, with explicit eviction. The503-word failure remains; fewer slots alone are not evidence of improvement.

Explicit source-word continuation already exists and the fixed learned-fragment models failed. The boundary mechanism here carries no novelty claim; the bounded dynamic notebook is the proposed distinction.
